landmarks.name: Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar
landmarks.description: The main entrance gate to Bandwar village. Built under the initiative of Girija Singh.

landmarks.name: Chandrashekhar Chowk
landmarks.description: The village square with the statue of Chandrashekhar Singh — Begusarai's first communist MLA.

landmarks.name: Shivala
landmarks.description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, in the centre of the village.

landmarks.name: Maharishi Gautam Aadi Shakti Durga Mandir
landmarks.description: A temple dedicated to Durga, featuring a Chaiti Durga idol. Orange exterior with green pillars.

landmarks.name: Bada Krishna Mandir
landmarks.description: The larger of the village's two Krishna temples.

landmarks.name: Chhota Krishna Mandir
landmarks.description: The smaller Krishna temple, with colorful arches and marble steps.

landmarks.name: Ram Mandir Thakurbari
landmarks.description: The village's Ram temple, with two shikharas. Site of the annual Ram Katha.

landmarks.name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Mandir
landmarks.description: A temple dedicated to Hanuman ji, with a red idol and brass bell.

landmarks.name: Baba Bhole Durgasthan Hanuman Mandir
landmarks.description: A mid-village temple dedicated to Baba Bhole, Durga, and Hanuman.

landmarks.name: State Bank of India — Bandwar Branch
landmarks.description: The village's only bank branch. IFSC: SBIN0015585. ATM also available.

landmarks.name: Ram Janki Fuels — IOCL Petrol Pump
landmarks.description: Indian Oil petrol pump on SH 55. Operated as Ram Janki Fuels.

landmarks.name: Bhagwandutt S.N.K. High School
landmarks.description: The village's first high school, established 1942 as a free Gurukul by Pandit Taradutt Pathak.

landmarks.name: High School UMV
landmarks.description: A high school in the Chak Parna area near Bandwar.

landmarks.name: Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya
landmarks.description: The government middle school, established 1955.

landmarks.name: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir
landmarks.description: A private school offering primary and upper primary education. Established 2015.

landmarks.name: Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya
landmarks.description: The village library on Bandwar Road, inaugurated by Rakesh Sinha ji. Built with MPLAD funds under the initiative of Girija Singh.

landmarks.name: Gram Panchayat Bhawan
landmarks.description: The office of the Bandwar Gram Panchayat.

landmarks.name: Burhi Gandak River
landmarks.description: The flood-prone river that flows along the western edge of Bandwar.

landmarks.name: Madhuri Dhala
landmarks.description: A road junction on the southern edge of Bandwar, where a village link road branches off from SH 55 (State Highway 55). It serves as a key turning point for residents and visitors travelling between Bandwar and the surrounding areas.

landmarks.name: Grace Brick Plant
landmarks.description: A brick manufacturing plant on the outskirts of Bandwar where Grace brand bricks are produced. It is a local industrial unit that supplies construction materials to the village and surrounding areas.

landmarks.name: HP Gas Gramin Vitrak
landmarks.description: An HP Gas (Hindustan Petroleum) rural LPG distributor serving Bandwar and nearby villages. Residents can book LPG cylinder refills, open new gas connections, and avail government LPG subsidy schemes through this distributor.

landmarks.name: Government Bamboo Exporting Plant
landmarks.description: A government-run bamboo facility in Bandwar where bamboo structures are crafted to protect newly planted saplings. The bamboo frames and guards produced here are used to shield young plants from damage, supporting the region's afforestation and plantation drives.

landmarks.name: Government Fertilizer Shop (PM-KISAN Urvarak)
landmarks.description: A licensed fertiliser outlet operating under the PM-KISAN Urvarak scheme. It supplies subsidised urea, DAP, NPK and potash to farmers in Bandwar and the surrounding area at government-controlled prices.

landmarks.name: Shivam Sudha Milk Parlour
landmarks.description: A Sudha dairy outlet in Bandwar selling milk, curd, paneer, ghee and sweets. It is the village's local point for packaged dairy products under the Bihar State Milk Co-operative Federation.
